tasks.title: sleep and elapsed
tasks.statement:
Remember Instant::now(), sleep for 100 ms with tokio::time::sleep and print "at least 100 ms passed: true" (compare elapsed() with Duration::from_millis(100)).

Expected output:
`at least 100 ms passed: true`
tasks.hint: start.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(100).

tasks.title: Fix it: blocking sleep
tasks.statement:
Three tasks sleep with the blocking std::thread::sleep on a single-threaded runtime, so they run one after another. Fix the program so that they sleep at the same time: the output must be "fast: true".

Expected output:
`fast: true`
tasks.hint: Replace std::thread::sleep(..) with tokio::time::sleep(..).await — the task will give up the thread.

tasks.title: Three sleeps at once
tasks.statement:
Use tokio::join! to run three 100 ms sleeps at the same time and print "in parallel: true" if everything took less than 200 ms.

Expected output:
`in parallel: true`
tasks.hint: join!(sleep(d), sleep(d), sleep(d)).await is enough: join! already returns a future, and you await it with .await.

tasks.title: sleep_until
tasks.statement:
Compute a deadline: Instant::now() + 120 ms, wait for it with sleep_until and print "deadline reached: true" (Instant::now() >= deadline).

Expected output:
`deadline reached: true`
tasks.hint: time::sleep_until(deadline).await.

tasks.title: Completion order
tasks.statement:
Start three tasks: «a» sleeps 60 ms, «b» 20 ms, «c» 40 ms; after its sleep each one prints its name. Wait for all of them. The sleeps determine the output order.

Expected output:
b
c
a
tasks.hint: For each task tokio::spawn(async move { sleep(..).await; println!(..) }); then .await each JoinHandle.

tasks.title: timeout: in time
tasks.statement:
Wrap an async block (sleep 20 ms, then return 5) in a 200 ms timeout and print the result with {:?}.

Expected output:
Ok(5)
tasks.hint: time::timeout(Duration, future).await returns Result<T, Elapsed>.

tasks.title: timeout: too late
tasks.statement:
Wrap a 200 ms sleep in a 30 ms timeout. If an error comes back, print it with {} (the Display of Elapsed).

Expected output:
deadline has elapsed
tasks.hint: if let Err(e) = r { println!("{}", e); }

tasks.title: Elapsed into your own error
tasks.statement:
Write async fn fetch() -> Result<u32, String>: it waits for a 200 ms sleep through a 30 ms timeout and turns Elapsed into the string "timeout" with map_err. Print the result with {:?}.

Expected output:
`Err("timeout")`
tasks.hint: time::timeout(..).await.map_err(|_| "timeout".to_string()) — you get a Result<(), String>.

tasks.title: Shared deadline
tasks.statement:
Set a deadline of "now + 100 ms". Perform two steps in a row, each a 60 ms sleep, and limit both with timeout_at(deadline, ..). For each one print "step N: ok" or "step N: expired".

Expected output:
`step 1: ok`
`step 2: expired`
tasks.hint: There is one deadline for both steps: the second step no longer makes it.

tasks.title: The first tick is immediate
tasks.statement:
Create an interval of 100 ms, wait for the first tick() and print "first tick immediately: true" if less than 30 ms passed.

Expected output:
`first tick immediately: true`
tasks.hint: time::interval(Duration) — the first tick() returns immediately.

tasks.title: Four ticks
tasks.statement:
An interval of 50 ms: wait for 4 ticks (the first is immediate). Print "4 ticks in 140–220 ms: true" if the total time falls in that range.

Expected output:
`4 ticks in 140–220 ms: true`
tasks.hint: Ticks at 0, 50, 100 and 150 ms — about 150 ms in total.

tasks.title: An interval without drift
tasks.statement:
Repeat 5 times: tick() of a 50 ms interval, then "work" (a 20 ms sleep). Print "no drift: true" if everything took less than 300 ms. (With sleep(50) instead of an interval it would take about 350 ms.)

Expected output:
`no drift: true`
tasks.hint: The interval's period is counted from the start, not from the end of the work.

tasks.title: MissedTickBehavior::Delay
tasks.statement:
An interval of 50 ms with MissedTickBehavior::Delay. Take the first tick, sleep for 120 ms (the ticks are late), take the second tick (it fires immediately), then measure the time until the third. Print "pause after being late: true" if it is at least 45 ms.

Expected output:
`pause after being late: true`
tasks.hint: iv.set_missed_tick_behavior(time::MissedTickBehavior::Delay).

tasks.title: MissedTickBehavior::Burst
tasks.statement:
The same scenario with the default behavior (Burst): the first tick, a 120 ms sleep, then two ticks in a row. Print "Burst in a row: true" if the second came less than 20 ms after the first of them.

Expected output:
`Burst in a row: true`
tasks.hint: Burst hands out the missed ticks without pauses to catch up with the schedule.

tasks.title: MissedTickBehavior::Skip
tasks.statement:
An interval of 50 ms with MissedTickBehavior::Skip. The first tick, a 120 ms sleep (the ticks at 50 and 100 are missed), then one tick() (it is late and fires immediately) and a measurement of the wait for the next tick(). Print "Skip waits for grid: true" if it is between 10 and 50 ms (until the tick at 150 ms).

Expected output:
`Skip waits for grid: true`
tasks.hint: Skip drops the missed ticks and waits for the nearest tick of the original grid.

tasks.title: reset of an interval
tasks.statement:
An interval of 100 ms: the first tick is immediate, sleep for 30 ms, call reset(), measure the next tick(). Print "after reset waited ≥ 90 ms: true".

Expected output:
`after reset waited ≥ 90 ms: true`
tasks.hint: reset() moves the next tick a full period from the current moment.

tasks.title: interval_at
tasks.statement:
Create interval_at(Instant::now() + 100 ms, 50 ms) and measure the first tick(). Print "first tick later: true" if at least 95 ms passed.

Expected output:
`first tick later: true`
tasks.hint: interval_at(start, period): the first tick is at the moment start.

tasks.title: Who is first
tasks.statement:
In select! wait for two sleeps: 20 ms (prints «a») and 100 ms (prints «b»). Only the first one runs.

Expected output:
a
tasks.hint: tokio::select! { _ = sleep(..) => println!(..), _ = sleep(..) => println!(..) }

tasks.title: select! as a timeout
tasks.statement:
In select! wait for a slow operation (an async block: sleep 200 ms, then return "done") and a 50 ms sleep. If the operation won, print its value; otherwise print "time-out".

Expected output:
`time-out`
tasks.hint: v = async { .. } => println!("{v}"), _ = sleep(..) => println!("time-out")

tasks.title: select! as an expression
tasks.statement:
Assign the result of select! to a variable: the first branch is an async block with a 30 ms sleep and the value 1, the second is a 10 ms sleep and the value 2. Print the variable.

Expected output:
2
tasks.hint: let r = tokio::select! { v = f1 => v, v = f2 => v };

tasks.title: The else branch
tasks.statement:
Declare let ready = false; and in select! put a branch with a 10 ms sleep and the condition `if ready`, plus an else branch. Print «else» from the else branch.

Expected output:
else
tasks.hint: _ = sleep(..), if ready => .., else => println!("else")

tasks.title: biased
tasks.statement:
In a loop of 100 iterations call select! with biased; and two branches that are ready at once (std::future::ready(())). Count how many times the first one won. Print "first branch: 100".

Expected output:
`first branch: 100`
tasks.hint: tokio::select! { biased; _ = ready(()) => first += 1, _ = ready(()) => {} }

tasks.title: A fair choice
tasks.statement:
Without biased;, in a loop of 1000 iterations call select! with two ready branches and count the wins of each. Print "both won: true" if both have more than zero wins.

Expected output:
`both won: true`
tasks.hint: By default the polling order is random, so both branches win.

tasks.title: The loser is dropped
tasks.statement:
Define a struct Guard(&'static str) with a Drop that prints "drop <name>". In select! the first branch is an async block: it creates Guard("slow") and sleeps for 200 ms; the second is a 10 ms sleep. After select! print "after select". Look at the order in which the lines appeared: the losing future (and the Guard with it) is dropped before that.

Expected output:
`drop slow`
`after select`
tasks.hint: The Guard lives inside the async block: it is released when the block is dropped.

tasks.title: Fix it: a sleep in a select! loop
tasks.statement:
A sender sends messages every 50 ms. The loop must stop 125 ms after the start, but the sleep is created anew on every iteration and never fires. Fix it: create the sleep before the loop, pin it (tokio::pin!) and pass it to select! by &mut. Expected "messages: 2".

Expected output:
`messages: 2`
tasks.hint: let deadline = sleep(..); tokio::pin!(deadline); and in select! — _ = &mut deadline => break.

tasks.title: recv is cancel safe
tasks.statement:
A sender sends the numbers 1, 2, 3 with a 40 ms pause and closes the channel. The receiver loops: select! between rx.recv() and a 15 ms sleep (the sleep only counts "empty" waits and drops recv). All messages must arrive. Print "received: 3".

Expected output:
`received: 3`
tasks.hint: recv() can be dropped safely: the message stays in the channel.

tasks.title: Retry with a growing pause
tasks.statement:
Write a retry: the operation fails on the first two attempts (Err("fail")) and succeeds on the third. After failures wait 20 ms, then 40 ms (doubling). For each attempt print "attempt N: fail" or "attempt N: ok", and at the end "waited at least 60 ms: true".

Expected output:
`attempt 1: fail`
`attempt 2: fail`
`attempt 3: ok`
`waited at least 60 ms: true`
tasks.hint: A loop over the attempts; after a failure sleep(delay).await and delay *= 2.

tasks.title: A timeout on each attempt
tasks.statement:
An operation attempt(n): the first two attempts sleep for 200 ms, the third returns 42 at once. Limit each attempt with a 50 ms timeout. Print "attempt N: timeout" or "attempt N: 42".

Expected output:
`attempt 1: timeout`
`attempt 2: timeout`
`attempt 3: 42`
tasks.hint: for n in 1..=3 { match timeout(.., attempt(n)).await { Ok(v) => .., Err(_) => .. } }

tasks.title: Nested timeouts
tasks.statement:
An inner 30 ms timeout wraps an 80 ms sleep, an outer 200 ms timeout wraps the inner one. Print "inner: expired, outer: ok".

Expected output:
`inner: expired, outer: ok`
tasks.hint: The outer one returns Ok(Err(Elapsed)): it made it in time itself, the inner one did not.

tasks.title: Heartbeat
tasks.statement:
In a select! loop combine a 100 ms interval (count the ticks) and a shared 250 ms deadline (a sleep pinned before the loop). When the deadline fires, exit and print "heartbeats: 3" (ticks at 0, 100 and 200 ms).

Expected output:
`heartbeats: 3`
tasks.hint: tokio::pin! for the deadline; in select! — _ = &mut deadline => break and _ = iv.tick() => n += 1.
